sec-head.p: Production builds matched to your architecture: retrieval-first, agent-first, or both.

card.p: An independent architecture assessment of your use case, data, and throughput requirements, resulting in a written recommendation: LangChain, LlamaIndex, or a hybrid, with latency and overhead benchmarks.
Retrieval-first builds: hierarchical chunking, auto-merging retrieval, and query synthesis for document-heavy applications where answer accuracy from your corpus is the product.
Multi-step agent systems: tool use, conversational memory, state management, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints for AI that takes actions, not just answers questions.
LlamaIndex as the retrieval layer wrapped as a tool inside a LangGraph agent, combining best-in-class retrieval with production-grade orchestration in one system.
Assessment and migration support for teams hitting friction from a wrong early choice, or needing to add agentic capability to an existing retrieval-only system.

card cta-card.p: Try the fit-check widget above, or get it scoped properly.

ul: Retrieval quality is the primary bottleneck, not orchestration complexity: hierarchical indices deliver 15-25% better answers on multi-source synthesis benchmarks vs. naive chunking.
You need complex multi-document reasoning: tree index and response synthesizers produce roughly 10-15% better answers on multi-source synthesis benchmarks.
Your documents are hierarchically structured (legal, code, technical manuals): composable indices produce roughly 15-25% better answers with lower memory overhead.
You want to ship faster with less code and lower latency overhead: LlamaIndex's auto-merging retrieval reduces query latency by 30-40% compared to manual LangChain RAG pipelines.

card.h3: RAG is one piece of a larger agent
ul: RAG is one component of a larger agentic system, not the whole product: LangGraph's multi-step agent graphs handle complex branching logic that LlamaIndex's linear pipelines cannot.
You need tool use, multi-step reasoning, or persistent memory across a conversation: LangGraph's state machine model supports checkpointing and interrupt/resume natively.
Human-in-the-loop checkpoints matter: LangGraph has native checkpointing and interrupt/resume support, critical for compliance-heavy workflows.
First-party observability (LangSmith) is a requirement, not an afterthought: LangSmith provides per-step latency traces and token usage, essential for debugging agent loops.
